prerequisites: Terrestrial and satellite radio communication systems

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamentals of radar, localization, and radionavigation systems.
Define the specifications of each of the communication subsystems that make up a radiolocation system.
Apply advanced digital processing techniques to radar and radionavigation systems.
Integrate technologies of radar and radionavigation systems.
Develop, coordinate, and direct a radiolocation systems project.
Effectively communicate the reasons and conclusions supporting decisions made in project development.
Apply acquired knowledge to solve new problems in radar, radiolocation, or radionavigation.
Autonomously study any future radar, radiolocation, or radionavigation system.
Define the specifications of each of the communication subsystems that make up a radiolocation system.
Apply advanced digital processing techniques to radar and radionavigation systems.
Integrate technologies of radar and radionavigation systems.
Elaborate, coordinate, and direct a radiolocation systems project.

syllabus_topics: Air navigation: PSR/SSR, VOR, DME, ILS
Short range: Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, IEEE 802.15.4 (UWB. Zigbee, 6LoWPAN)
Cellular and wireless network-based radiolocation architecture and subsystems
Definition of applications/use cases and technical requirements
Software development: interfaces, algorithms, software testing

assessment_methods.method: Practical work (P1) on first laboratory practice
Practical work (P2) on second laboratory practice
Practical work (P3) on classroom practices and third laboratory practice (project planning and execution)

assessment_rules: The theoretical block grade is 1 * T1. The practical block grade is (0.2 * P1) + (0.2 * P2) + (0.6 * P3). The final grade for the ordinary call is (0.4 * Theoretical block grade) + (0.6 * Practical block grade). To pass, the sum of theoretical and practical grades must be 5 or greater. For the extraordinary call, students can retake a theoretical exam and a practical exam, or keep their ordinary practical grade; retaking the practical exam implies waiving the ordinary practical grade. In case of doubt about authorship, students may be required to defend their work.
